html:
An army officer who seized power in Guinea on 3 April 1984, a week after the death of Sekou Toure, and ruled until his own death in December 2008.

He freed the prisoners of Camp Boiro, brought back private trade and the Guinean franc, and opened the country to the West. From 1993 he won multiparty elections that opponents called rigged. Guinea stayed stable while war spread in Sierra Leone and Liberia next door, and it took in hundreds of thousands of refugees. His last years saw strikes, a failing economy and his own illness. Within hours of his death, officers led by Moussa Dadis Camara took power.
sum: An army officer who seized power in Guinea on 3 April 1984, a week after the death of Sekou Toure, and ruled until his own death in December 2008.
